transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s been going on a while. Almost two years.

After a commission I did, I started noticing people in the ensemble changing schedules, where people were seated, little comments in rehearsals… it felt like they were quietly trying to undermine my work. They’ll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, but I still can’t really shake the feeling that there’s more to it.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is there?
No… I don’t think so. Not voices like that.
Do you believe for certain that these people are deliberately trying to undermine you?

Certain is a strong word… but yes, it feels that way. I keep trying to talk myself out of it, especially when they show me emails or explanations, but I still can’t shake that it’s deliberate—like the schedule changes and seating choices after that commission were meant to undercut me.
Outside of this ensemble, do you generally find it hard to trust other people’s motives?

Not really… not in general. It’s mostly around the ensemble, after that commission. A few people there—schedule changes, seating things, comments in rehearsal—it just feels hard to believe it’s all innocent, even when they show me emails or notes.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by someone or something outside you?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get stuck on certain thoughts, but they still feel like mine.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or seems disorganized?
Not really. I mean… maybe someone’s asked me to repeat myself if I’m rushing, but I don’t think people have said I’m hard to follow or anything like that.
Have you ever felt that ordinary things around you—like comments, gestures, or events—were sending you special messages meant specifically for you?

Sort of… not like street signs or anything. More like in rehearsals, little comments or seating changes, schedule changes. After that commission, it started feeling like some of those things were aimed at me, like a few people were trying to make a point or quietly undercut what I was doing. Even when they had explanations for it, I couldn’t really shake that feeling.
Even when people show you clear evidence that there was an innocent reason, are you able to accept that explanation?

I can hear the explanation, and sometimes it makes sense on paper. But… no, not really. Even when they show me emails or rehearsal notes, I still feel pretty certain there’s something behind the schedule changes or seating choices or those little comments. It’s hard for me to let it go.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?
No… I don’t think so. Nothing like seeing things other people couldn’t see.
Over the past two years, have you found yourself losing motivation or emotional expressiveness compared with how you used to be?
I’m not sure. I mean… I still do my work. I don’t think I’ve become flat or anything like that. Maybe I’m quieter sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a big change.
Have you ever believed that other people could read your thoughts?

No… not read my thoughts. It’s more that I feel certain some people in the ensemble have been quietly working against me through things like schedule changes or little comments. But not like they can hear what I’m thinking.
Have you become much less interested in spending time with other people than you used to be?
Not really. I mean, I still see people when I need to. Maybe I keep to myself a bit more sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in people.
Aside from the ensemble situation, have you had any other beliefs that other people would say are unusual or hard to believe?

Not really outside of that. It’s mostly… that situation. Since the commission, I’ve just been pretty sure a few of them were using schedule changes, seating decisions, little remarks in rehearsal—things like that—to undercut what I was doing. Even when they’d show me emails or notes explaining it, it didn’t really feel like the full story.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about the ensemble trying to undermine you?

I mean… I suppose anything is possible. But it doesn’t feel like I’m mistaken. It’s been almost two years, and I still can’t really shake the sense that after the commission, a few of them started using those schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to undermine me. Even when they show emails or notes explaining it, I just… don’t feel like that’s the whole story.
Do you ever think there is a real chance that your suspicion about the ensemble could be false?

I guess there’s always a chance, technically. But no… it doesn’t really feel false to me. I’ve been stuck on it for almost two years now, and even when they show me emails or notes, I still feel like there’s something else going on.
If someone proved to you beyond doubt that the schedule changes and comments were innocent, would you still believe the ensemble was trying to undermine you?

I don’t know. If it was really beyond doubt, I’d have to look at it, I guess. But… honestly, I think I’d still have a hard time shaking the feeling that something was going on. It’s been there for almost two years.
Have you ever behaved in a way that other people saw as very strange or disorganized?
I don’t think so. I mean, people have said I’m withdrawn or intense sometimes, but… strange or disorganized? Not that I’m aware of.
Because of this situation, has your ability to work or manage your usual life dropped a lot compared with before?

Not a lot, no. I mean, this whole thing affects me, but outside of the ensemble situation I’m still getting my work done. I meet deadlines, keep composing, run most mornings… things with my wife are basically steady. So I wouldn’t say my whole life has fallen apart.
Are you absolutely convinced that the ensemble has been trying to undermine you?

Yes. I mean… I know how it sounds, but I’m pretty convinced. Even when they show me emails or notes explaining the schedule changes or seating, it doesn’t really change the feeling that a few of them have been quietly trying to undermine my work since that commission.
When you’re around unfamiliar people, do you feel very anxious because you fear they may have bad intentions toward you?
Not really. I can be a bit guarded with people I don’t know, but I wouldn’t say I’m very anxious or assume they mean me harm.

There are no hallucinations, thought control, thought broadcasting, disorganized speech/behavior, negative symptoms, or marked functional decline, making delusional disorder more likely than schizophrenia.
